title: The Fall of Constantinople
objective: After this level you can explain how the Ottomans took Constantinople in 1453.
summary: In 1453 the 21-year-old Sultan Mehmed II broke Constantinople's walls with Urban's cannon, hauled ships overland past the harbor chain, took the city on 29 May and made it his capital.

cards.headline: Level 4’s land walls had stood since 412. In 1453 a young sultan brought cannon.
cards.body: His name was Mehmed II, and he was 21. How did he take the city nobody could take?

cards.headline: A gunsmith named Urban
cards.body: Mehmed hired a Hungarian gunsmith, Urban, to build cannon powerful enough to bring the walls down. From 6 April 1453 the guns pounded away. Between 60,000 and 80,000 Ottoman soldiers, with 69 cannon, faced only 6,000 to 7,000 trained defenders. Remember Level 4’s moat, outer wall and main wall? Cannon didn’t have to climb them. It battered a breach straight through.

cards.headline: Ships over the hill
cards.body: The city’s harbor, the Golden Horn, was sealed by a great chain. Mehmed’s answer: go around it. His men built an oiled wooden ramp and hauled smaller ships overland, and by 22 April they were inside, past the chain. If the door is locked, carry the boat around the house.

mascot.line: Nobody guards the hillside against boats. That was rather the point.

cards.headline: 29 May 1453
cards.body: The final assault came in the early hours of 29 May. The last emperor, Constantine XI, is reported to have been killed, either fighting near the breach or fleeing. Mehmed rode to Hagia Sophia, Level 5’s great church, and converted it into a mosque. He moved his capital from Edirne to Constantinople, and the Byzantine Empire came to an end.

cards.headline: Constantinople 1453: understood
learned: Mehmed II was 21 when he took the city
Urban’s cannon pounded the land walls
Ships were hauled overland past the chain
Hagia Sophia became a mosque; Byzantium ended

questions.prompt: Constantinople’s layered walls had held for centuries. What did Mehmed II hire the gunsmith Urban to build?

options.label: Siege towers taller than the walls
Cannon powerful enough to bring the walls down

questions.explanation: Mehmed hired the Hungarian gunsmith Urban to build cannon that could bring down the walls.

questions.prompt: How did Mehmed’s ships get past the chain across the Golden Horn?

options.label: They broke the chain with cannon fire
They were hauled overland on an oiled ramp
Divers cut the chain at night
The defenders lowered it by mistake

questions.explanation: Mehmed had smaller ships hauled overland on an oiled wooden ramp, and by 22 April they were past the chain.

questions.prompt: What happened to Justinian’s Hagia Sophia after Constantinople fell in 1453?

options.label: Mehmed converted it into a mosque
It was pulled down to build a palace
options.rationale: It survived, with a new purpose.

options.label: It was left empty for centuries
options.rationale: Mehmed rode straight to it and converted it.

questions.explanation: Mehmed rode to Hagia Sophia and converted it into a mosque.
